strongest_counterclaim: The claim that Lane carries limited independent information in constructive pullback weeks is essentially unfalsifiable on the evidence presented. The 27-case failure archaeology is a conditional-on-error subset, the constructive-pullback slice inside it is probably n<=15, the proposed quintile-matching protocol has insufficient resolution to detect a 3-6pp effect, and the technical features used as 'controls' are themselves mediators/downstream readouts of the same leadership dimension Lane encodes. The prior researcher has not refuted Lane-independence; they have merely failed to measure it with a design capable of doing so.

attacks.issue: Selection-on-error sampling: the entire evidence base is a 'failure archaeology' pool — every case is pre-classified as something the system got wrong or right in an extreme way. Constructing a 'redundancy' claim from a sample where winners and ruin-cases are over-sampled relative to the natural base rate is a textbook conditional-on-outcome bias.
attacks.why_it_matters: If Lane is calibrated to suppress mid-decile setups, the failure archaeology is by construction enriched for cases at the tails of Lane's discrimination boundary. That is precisely where Lane-noise dominates — the wrong test to ask whether Lane has mean-shift information.

attacks.issue: Endogeneity / collider bias: ma10_slope_5, mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50, and pullback geometry are not exogenous covariates relative to Lane — they are partial proxies of the same underlying accumulation/leadership state that Lane is designed to read. Conditioning on them and testing Lane's residual is conditioning on mediators of Lane.
attacks.why_it_matters: If Lane = f(leadership, accumulation, RS-trend, sector-context) and the technicals are g(leadership), then the residual of Lane | technicals is not 'independent Lane information' but 'Lane information not yet captured by a subset of its inputs'. Claiming that residual must be zero is begging the question.

attacks.issue: Insufficient power / unstable standardized deltas: numeric_contrasts are computed on n=5 (false_negative) vs n=11 (selected_winner). With these sample sizes, a single case flip changes standardized_delta by ~0.3-0.4. The reported |z|>0.6 deltas are not statistically meaningful; bootstrap CIs would span zero on most features.
attacks.why_it_matters: The 'directional leadership proxies' the prior researcher concedes Lane 'could encode independently' are exactly the dimensions the noisy contrasts fail to rule out. The hedge in their evidence_against is actually the honest reading of the data.

attacks.issue: Quintile-matching is too coarse to test the discrimination claim. ma10_slope_5 spans roughly -0.005 to 0.09 in the sample; quintiles compress ~0.02-wide bands where within-bin residual variation in W4 outcomes is far larger than any plausible Lane effect (3-6pp).
attacks.why_it_matters: A 3pp hit-rate gap easily drowns in within-quintile outcome noise. The falsifiable_prediction '<3pp means indifference' would be triggered by random within-bin variation, not by true Lane-nullity. The bar is set where any reasonable test would always fail.

attacks.issue: Spearman(SCORE_BEFORE_LANE, post-Lane) >0.70 in n<30 is not a discriminative threshold — with that sample size, correlations of 0.65-0.85 arise routinely from noise, especially when both scores share many of the same input features (mom, slope, RS).
attacks.why_it_matters: This test cannot distinguish 'Lane is redundant' from 'Lane and pre-Lane composite share so many inputs that high correlation is mechanical'. The number is uninformative regardless of which side of 0.70 the data lands.

attacks.issue: Omitted-variable bias on sector and market regime: every case in the failure archaeology is associated with a snapshot id, several of which cluster (e.g., snap_71486ed83c has 6 cases; snap_d0d57b1e40 has 5). The shared-snapshot clustering means sector/market-regime effects are confounded with Lane assignment.
attacks.why_it_matters: If a single snapshot contributes both a B0 constructive-pullback pick and a not-B0 LANE_NEUTRAL pick, and the outcome gap tracks the snapshot, that is regime — not Lane. The prior analysis does not partial out snapshot-fixed-effects, which inflates any apparent Lane-noise reading.

attacks.issue: The mixed-label case entity_6618d3e80c (false_positive_ruin|selected_winner, px_vs_ma50=0.337, mom_20=0.251) is direct evidence that Lane correctly identified an extreme-leadership constructive pullback that the standard technical composite would have weighted similarly to entity_3adc078f01 (snap_ad495b6705, mom_20=0.172, large_win). Lane adds the RS-trend read the technicals miss.
attacks.why_it_matters: The prior researcher's own cited case cuts against their conclusion. They hand-wave it as 'Lane can resolve genuine strong leadership' but then conclude Lane is mostly redundant in this regime — that is internally inconsistent.

attacks.issue: The 'constructive pullback' definition itself is partly Lane-derivable: pullback_duration_weeks 3-9 and pullback_pct -5 to -25 with positive slopes and px_vs_ma20>0 is the canonical 'healthy basing' read, which is exactly what Lane is engineered to endorse. Restricting to this band and then testing Lane's independence is a circular conditioning set.
attacks.why_it_matters: The very filter that defines the regime is the type of pattern Lane is designed to confirm. Any signal Lane adds inside this band will look like restatement, by construction.

counterexamples_to_seek: Constructive pullback weeks where ma10_slope_5, mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, pullback_duration_weeks, and pullback_pct are matched to <0.005 / <0.01 / <0.05 / <1wk / <1pp tolerance between B0_LANE and LANE_NEUTRAL cases — does W4-return distribution still overlap, or does Lane split them? This is the only design that can answer the question.

Constructive pullbacks with px_vs_ma50 in the top decile (>0.20) where Lane is the differentiator between entity_6618d3e80c-style extreme-RS and entity_3adc078f01-style moderate-RS cases — does Lane separate them on forward W4 in a held-out window?

Constructive pullbacks split by pullback_duration_weeks: 3-5wk shallow vs 7-9wk deep — does Lane's information content differ between shallow-base and deep-base subregimes? (The shallow-base Lane calls may be noisier than the deep-base Lane calls, which would actually argue for keeping Lane precisely where the prior researcher says to remove it.)

Constructive pullbacks conditioned on up_day_ratio_20 above 0.60 — does Lane still separate winners from ruins, or do all high-up-day-ratio constructive pullbacks perform similarly regardless of Lane? If similarly, the prior claim strengthens; if not, Lane is independently informative.

Constructive pullbacks in which the technical composite scores identically across B0_LANE and LANE_NEUTRAL but the entity has different IBD-style RS-trend trajectory (3-month RS slope) — does Lane's match to RS-trend predict the W4 outcome better than the technical composite alone?

Cross-snapshot replication: take the snap_71486ed83c cluster (6 cases), hold it out, and re-derive the W4 separation. If the pattern is snapshot-specific, the 'Lane is noise' reading is actually a 'regime is noise' reading.
what_would_change_my_mind: A matched-cohort test with n>=100 constructive-pullback cases where B0_LANE and LANE_NEUTRAL are matched within tolerance bands of <0.01 on ma10_slope_5, <0.03 on mom_20, <0.05 on up_day_ratio_20, <1wk on pullback_duration, <3pp on pullback_pct — and a Cox/Hazard model with Lane as the only remaining predictor shows hazard-ratio p-value >0.4 in a held-out fold. Anything weaker than this is consistent with my prior that the current evidence is inconclusive.

A principal-component / factor-loading analysis where Lane collapses onto the first PC of (mom_20, mom_60, ma10_slope_5, ma20_slope_5, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma20, px_vs_ma50, RS-trend) at loading >0.75 AND the residual after projection is orthogonal to W4-return — both conditions must hold for the redundancy claim to be defensible.

A pre-registered A/B backtest in constructive-pullback weeks showing that the policy 'ignore Lane when constructive-pullback gate fires' improves Sharpe/Sharpe-ratio-of-returns net of slippage by >0.05 over 'keep Lane' on out-of-sample folds, with the gain surviving bootstrap CIs. Backtest-only claims without the matched-cohort step are not sufficient.

A demonstration that within the constructive-pullback subset, the cases Lane rejects (LANE_NEUTRAL or no-B0) have identical forward W4 distributions to the cases Lane accepts, after controlling for pullback_duration_weeks AND base_depth_pct AND dist_to_52w_high_pct simultaneously — not just the four features the prior researcher listed.
Until any of the above is produced, the honest verdict is UNRESOLVED, not 'Lane is redundant in constructive pullbacks'.
